title: Decentralized probe aggregation and adaptive throttling to stabilize autoscaling and SLOs
creator: Riley Chen
description: Goal: Improve autoscaler stability and SLO preservation during partial-region degradations by moving from centralized probe ingestion to a decentralized, local-aggregation model with adaptive throttling and token-aware derating. Background: Our centralized health pipeline has caused amplified noise during transient failures (traffic spikes, GC storms, intermittent infra glitches), triggering autoscaler thrash and unintended cross-region failovers. This leads to higher p99 latency and transient SLO breaches for critical customers. Proposal summary: 1) Deploy lightweight probe aggregators in each region/zone that compute regional health summaries (weighted success ratio, latency percentiles, error gradients) on sliding windows. 2) Use a small set of compact signals (health_score, short_term_trend, token_weighted_error) instead of raw probe fanout to global control plane. 3) Introduce an adaptive throttling controller co-located with the autoscaler that:   - applies token-aware derating (high-priority tokens reduce derating probability)   - uses stochastic smoothing to avoid step changes in readiness decisions   - gates circuit-breaker activation by confidence windows to prevent flapping 4) Add a local soft-fallback policy: when regional health is borderline, prefer local graceful degradation (reject low-priority/interruptible requests, downgrade batch sizes, enable KV-cache bypass) rather than immediate scale-up or cross-region failover. 5) Metrics and observability: expose health_score, derating_action, throttled_tokens, and local_autoscale_decision to the Console with a per-route SLO dashboard and alerting rules. Design considerations and trade-offs: - Decentralization reduces probe fanout and latency in decisioning but increases local complexity and release surface. - Stochastic smoothing sacrifices some reactivity for stability; we tune smoothing windows by traffic shape. - Token-aware derating requires accurate token-priority mapping from the API gateway; we will read a lightweight token header added by the edge. - We must keep the global control plane informed via periodic summaries to preserve cross-region decisions and global rollouts. Rollout plan: Phase A (canary region): implement aggregator binary + adaptive controller feature flag in us-west-2 for non-critical routes. Phase B (priority-aware): enable token-weighting for internal and enterprise tokens only. Phase C (global): enable for all regions with automated canary checks and runbook. Metrics to validate success: - Reduce autoscaler thrash events by >= 50% (defined as scale-ups followed by scale-downs within 10m) - Reduce SLO breach windows during regional incidents by >= 70% - Maintain p99 latency within existing SLOs for high-priority tokens - No net increase in steady-state cost beyond 5% Test plan: - Unit tests for aggregator math and smoothing kernel - Staging run with synthetic bubble tests (traffic-contracts) and injected latency/partial drop scenarios - Chaos test: kill a subset of serving nodes and assert local derating triggers before cross-region failover - Load test with token mix to validate priority-aware behavior Rollback and runbook: - Feature flags for aggregator and adaptive controller to disable in 1-min window - Escalation path to revert token header usage at the gateway if token mappings are inconsistent - Playbook pages: link to incident runbook and synthetic-transaction dashboard (Console) Links and artifacts: - Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/decen-probe-agg (internal) - Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2449 - Synthetic harness job: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/region-health-sim-2026-02 - Console dashboard draft: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/slo-region-health Comments: see comments array for ongoing discussion.
acceptance_criteria: Regional aggregator deployed behind feature flag and computing health_score at 30s and 5m windows
Adaptive throttling controller respects token priority and demonstrates <50% autoscaler thrash in canary region
Circuit-breaker activation requires 3 consecutive high-confidence health windows to prevent flips
Local soft-fallback prevents cross-region failover for at least 90% of simulated partial degradations in canary
Telemetry for health_score, derating_action, throttled_tokens, and autoscale_decision visible in Console and has alert rules
steps: Proto: implement aggregator server and smoothing kernel in runtime agent
Integrate token-priority header consumption at edge and surface to aggregator
Build adaptive controller module and unit tests
Wire aggregator summaries to global control plane with periodic heartbeat (rate-limited)
Canary deploy to us-west-2 for five non-critical routes and run synthetic incident suite
Iterate on smoothing windows and derating thresholds based on canary telemetry
Roll out token-aware derating for enterprise tokens, monitor, then expand
